title: Vithal Dayaji Temple, Sulewadi
tagline: Ancient basalt stone temple sanctum and architectural gem of Solapur district

heroImage.alt: Ancient stone temple ruins featuring intricate columns and architecture in Maharashtra

overview.description: Vithal Dayaji Temple in Sulewadi is a historic Hindu shrine located in the drought-prone rural plains of Solapur district, Maharashtra. Dedicated to Lord Vitthal (a beloved manifestation of Vishnu widely revered in Maharashtra), the temple stands as an evocative testament to Deccan basalt stone craftsmanship, featuring weathered pillars, a sanctum sanctorum, and deep cultural ties to the centuries-old Pandharpur Wari pilgrimage corridor.
overview.history: Believed to date back to the late medieval era when local pastoral and farming communities erected stone shrines honoring Vitthal and Dayaji, the temple served as a sanctuary for resting pilgrims marching along historic routes toward Pandharpur. The weathered basalt blocks, simple mandapa pillars, and secluded rural precinct reflect vernacular architectural heritage typical of the Solapur region.
overview.significance: The temple holds immense spiritual significance for local rural devotees and pilgrims who commemorate the saint-poet tradition of Maharashtra. It provides a peaceful, meditative atmosphere away from crowded commercial pilgrimage hubs.
overview.bestTimeToVisit: October to February when temperatures are pleasant and rural Solapur experiences mild winter weather.
overview.dressCode: Modest traditional attire suitable for a sacred Hindu shrine.

bestTime.description: Winter months offer cool mornings and evenings, making travel through rural Solapur comfortable.

howToReach.byAir: Pune International Airport (PNQ) is the nearest major airport (~190 km away) with regular domestic flights.
howToReach.byRail: Kurduvadi Junction (KWV, ~35 km) and Solapur Railway Station (SUR, ~75 km) are the closest well-connected railheads.
howToReach.byRoad: Accessible via state highways connecting Pandharpur, Malshiras, and Mohol. State transport buses and private taxis ply regularly.

faq.q: What is the significance of Vithal Dayaji Temple?
faq.a: It is a revered historic shrine in Solapur district dedicated to Lord Vitthal, celebrated for its basalt stone construction and connection to rural pilgrimage routes.
Sulewadi is accessible by road from Kurduvadi Junction (35 km) or Pandharpur (30 km). State buses and taxis operate along the route.

faq.q: Are there entry fees or photography restrictions?
faq.a: Entry is free. Photography of the exterior stone architecture is permitted, while maintaining sanctity within the inner sanctum.
